recipes.title: How To Reverse Sear A Steak

ingredients.name: thick-cut steaks (ribeye, NY strip, or filet mignon, at least 1.5 to 2 inches thick)
high smoke-point oil (canola, avocado, or grapeseed oil)

steps: Pat the steaks completely dry with paper towels, then season generously on all sides with kosher salt and cracked black pepper.
Set a wire rack inside a rimmed baking sheet and arrange steaks on top of the rack.

Bake in the preheated oven for 25 to 45 minutes, monitoring with an instant-read probe thermometer until target internal pull temperature is reached (110°F for rare, 120°F for medium-rare, 130°F for medium).
Heat high smoke-point cooking oil in a heavy cast iron skillet over high heat until smoking.
Transfer steaks to the hot skillet and sear for 1 minute on the first side.
Flip the steaks, immediately drop the butter, smashed garlic cloves, and herb sprigs into the pan.
Tilt the skillet and rapidly spoon the foaming herb butter over the tops of the steaks for 1 minute until a crisp, deep mahogany crust forms.
Sear the fat caps and edges with tongs for 30 seconds, then transfer steaks to a warm board to rest for 5 to 7 minutes before slicing.
recipes.swaps: Applicable to bone-in or boneless cuts; beef tallow can replace butter for high-heat basting.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Rimmed baking sheet, wire roasting rack, cast iron skillet, instant-read probe thermometer. Ideal for cuts 1.5 inches thick or greater.

recipes.title: Perfect Sous Vide Steak with Cast-Iron Herb Butter Sear

ingredients.name: New York strip steaks (1.5 inches thick, approx 1 lb each)
high smoke-point olive oil or avocado oil

steps: Set up an immersion circulator in a large pot filled with water. Preheat the water bath to 130°F-134°F for medium-rare (or 135°F-144°F for medium).
Pat strip steaks thoroughly dry with paper towels, then season both sides generously with coarse sea salt and coarse black pepper.
Place each steak into its own vacuum seal or silicone bag, adding 1 tablespoon of butter and 1 fresh herb sprig on top of each steak.
Seal the bags, removing as much air as possible (using vacuum sealer or water displacement method).
Submerge bags in preheated water bath and cook for 2 hours (up to 4 hours maximum).
Remove steaks from bags, discard cooking juices and herb sprigs, and pat both sides completely dry with paper towels (dry meat ensures a rapid sear).
Heat a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat until lightly smoking; add cooking oil.
Place steaks in the hot skillet and sear undisturbed for 1 minute on the first side.
Flip steaks and sear for 1 minute on the second side while spooning melted pan fat over top.
Transfer steaks to a cutting board, rest for 2 to 3 minutes, then slice against the grain and serve.
recipes.swaps: Ribeye or filet mignon can replace NY strip steaks; beef tallow can replace butter for searing.
recipes.notes: Equipment: Sous vide immersion circulator, large pot, sealable cooking bags, cast iron skillet, paper towels.
